touches.text: A ticket's code is a tool or machine; its life is data. All of its state is on disk, so anyone can instantiate it to talk to it, and any dialog is written to the relevant part of the ticket as it happens. To cross a gate the ticket asks that gate to queue it, sending only its fileref: devices/codemother/0/machines/<inspector>/queueme <fileref>. The gate instantiates the ticket from that fileref on its own side. A ticket instance then processes the pass or fail: on a pass it goes on to the next step, alerting the probes watching the gate (3.3.4.2); on a fail it asks design to queue it, the same way. Self-queuing is the abstract ticket's (3.3.2), so every kind inherits it and no caller queues a ticket on its behalf (Akien, same day: "that could be in the class, rather than the instance :) self queuing"). WHY: Akien, 2026-11-10: "now it has to send it's fileref over to the thing that will process it, and a new code instance created over there even tho it's the same thing... because that's good encapsulation. :)"
Commit often. WHY: so we never wind up with stray files or incomplete work.

More than one builder works on one box, and there will be more than two, so the whole-tree rule (a PROVEME crossing refuses while anything in either tree is uncommitted, working_tree_clean) is re-examined for N builders on a box. One builder's work must not block another's crossing. Akien 2026-11-13, answering Q#94 (measured 2026-11-12: 3195b3b834bc refused twice over d692ef650534's records; measured 2026-11-13: 46851816800f refused over ~330 paths of an unrelated merge commit, with four peers idle about an hour): "then it's time to reexamine that specific tooth given that you now have two builders on the box. because if we keep going, there'll be more than two..."

It is the READY TO MERGE ONTO MAIN step of the pipeline: everything's proved, and merging implies pushing it up. With a branch per ticket (3.3.6), commits on the branch are as often as we like; the inspector is the step at ready to merge. Checking what a change touched belongs here; nothing hangs off the git post-commit hook.

artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). WHY: errors are permanent in records of truth (Law 7), and the journal is what shows a record moved by hand. USERS: everyone who writes a record.
